guardian.title: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo now deadliest in country’s history
guardian.description:
At least 2,325 people have died from the virus, according to official data, with outbreak on track to be biggest in history

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is now the deadliest in the country’s history with at least 2,325 people dead, according to government data, surpassing the toll from the 2018-20 outbreak.

The DRC’s public health institute said confirmed cases had risen to 4,945, including 101 detected in the previous 24 hours.

guardian.title: Zimbabwe boat accident death toll hits 68 as 22 more bodies recovered
guardian.description:
Eighteen children among the people killed after ferry capsized on Lake Kariba

Twenty-two more bodies have been recovered after a boat accident in Zimbabwe, taking the death toll to 68, police said on Saturday.

The ferry capsized on Tuesday on Lake Kariba, on the border with Zambia. An investigation has suggested it was overloaded when it turned over during heavy winds.

An American missionary who was kidnapped in Niger in October has been released, his organisation has said.

Serving in Mission International said Kevin Rideout “is in good health in the care of US officials” and would soon be reunited with his extended family.

BP has answered Donald Trump’s call for oil companies to help rebuild Venezuela’s fossil fuel industry with new plans to develop a large offshore gasfield.

guardian.description:
Searchers dig through collapsed buildings and debris after 7.7 magnitude quake killed at least 53 people

Rescue crews dug through collapsed buildings and landslide debris in eastern Indonesia on Sunday as they searched for bodies and possible survivors a day after a powerful earthquake killed at least 53 people, injured more than 100 and displaced thousands.

guardian.description:
Quake struck Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground for fear of a tsunami

A 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck eastern Indonesia has killed at least 47 people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly seismic events.

Rescuers have yet to reach Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, because roads were blocked by landslides and communications disrupted.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, incendies et canicule : « Nous n’avons strictement rien à cacher », affirme Sébastien Lecornu en Gironde
lemonde.description: Le chef du gouvernement a fustigé les « dérives complotistes » au sujet des incendies dans les Landes et en Gironde. Une conférence de presse est prévue à 13 heures.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : un drôle de consensus pour le référendum
lemonde.description: Dans la foulée du Rassemblement national, qui promet depuis longtemps de le mettre en œuvre, les candidats à l’élection présidentielle semblent redécouvrir l’instrument de la démocratie directe, y compris à gauche et au centre. Comme remède à la crise de la légitimité présidentielle et à l’impuissance du politique.

lemonde.title: Au Liban, des frappes israéliennes meurtrières fragilisent un peu plus le cessez-le-feu avec le Hezbollah
lemonde.description: Alors que la mise en œuvre de l’accord-cadre signé avec Beyrouth est enlisée, l’armée israélienne a tué 11 personnes dans des bombardements autour de la ville de Nabatiyé, le 15 août, en riposte à une attaque contre ses soldats stationnés dans le sud du pays.

lemonde.title: Guerre en Ukraine : au cœur de la nuit, avec le régiment de drones qui frappe durement Moscou
lemonde.description: Le 413ᵉ régiment des forces sans pilote multiplie les attaques dans la grande profondeur depuis le territoire ukrainien. Kiev accélère ses efforts militaires pour porter le feu au cœur de l’appareil économique de son envahisseur.

lemonde.title: En Corée du Sud, malgré les atermoiements des Etats-Unis, des manœuvres conjointes pour faire face à l’« évolution de la nature de la guerre »
lemonde.description: Les traditionnels exercices conjoints entre Américains et Sud-Coréens sont programmés du 17 au 27 août. Même si Donald Trump a demandé à les « réduire considérablement », dimanche, en raison de son « excellente relation » avec le dirigeant nord-coréen, l’objectif est de se préparer à un conflit moderne, comme Pyongyang le fait aux côtés de la Russie.

lemonde.title: Olivier Nora crée sa propre maison d’édition, quatre mois après son éviction de la présidence de Grasset
lemonde.description: La nouvelle entité, Olivier Nora Editions, dans laquelle Editis prend une participation minoritaire, a vocation à publier, dès janvier 2027, entre une trentaine et une cinquantaine de titres par an.

lemonde.title: Ebola en RDC : l’épidémie devient la plus meurtrière de l’histoire du pays en seulement trois mois
lemonde.description: Sur les 4 945 cas de contaminations confirmées, 2 325 personnes sont mortes, selon le dernier bilan des autorités congolaises.

lemonde.title: Hayden Panettiere, révélée par les séries « Heroes » et « Nashville », est morte à l’âge de 36 ans
lemonde.description: La comédienne américaine, qui s’était fait connaître dès l’enfance avant d’accéder à la notoriété internationale grâce à « Heroes », est morte, dans des circonstances non communiquées. Son père a salué la mémoire d’une femme « rayonnante » ayant apporté « un amour et une joie immenses » à son entourage comme à ses millions de spectateurs.

lemonde.title: Le coût de la vie étudiante a augmenté de 1,66 % sur un an, et de plus de 35 % depuis l’élection d’Emmanuel Macron en 2017, alerte l’Unef
lemonde.description: Etudier coûte deux fois plus cher pour les étudiants étrangers extracommunautaires, « premières victimes des politiques austéritaires du gouvernement », pointe également l’enquête du syndicat étudiant, tandis que les étudiants des outre-mer, « grands oubliés des politiques publiques », déboursent entre 314 et 408 euros de plus par an que les étudiants de l’Hexagone.

lemonde.title: Collision de bateaux à Cannes : un disparu et dix blessés à la suite d’une collision entre deux bateaux de plaisance, les recherches reprennent
lemonde.description: Lors du choc, dix personnes, dont plusieurs adolescents, ont été blessées. Six sont en urgence relative, quatre en urgence absolue, et un homme de 24 ans est porté disparu.

lemonde.title: Trois kiosques gourmands pour manger sur le pouce cet été, de Calais à Marseille
lemonde.description: Partout en France, des cabanes proposent une spécialité locale pour combler un petit creux, qui font le bonheur des vacanciers. Détour par Calais, Marseille et Vannes.

lemonde.title: Aux championnats d’Europe 2026 de natation, un bilan en demi-teinte pour une équipe de France qui a vu éclore de nouvelles individualités prometteuses
lemonde.description: Après deux semaines de compétition à Paris et à Saint-Denis, l’Euro s’est achevé, dimanche, avec notamment le sacre de Léon Marchand sur 400 m nage libre, qui rehausse les performances des Bleus.

lemonde.title: Mortalité infantile : « Le débat se concentre sur l’organisation des maternités, alors que les déterminants sont ailleurs »
lemonde.description: Si la restructuration de l’offre obstétricale est indispensable, l’organisation et la qualité des soins délivrés aux grands prématurés représentent un enjeu central et largement oublié, estiment la présidente de SOS Préma, Charlotte Bouvard, et le pédiatre Jean-Christophe Rozé, dans une tribune au « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Championnat d’Europe d’athlétisme 2026 : aucun titre mais de « belles surprises », le bilan mitigé de l’équipe de France
lemonde.description: La délégation bleue repart de Birmingham avec onze médailles, loin des seize podiums, dont quatre titres, de la précédente édition de l’Euro. Mais le bilan offre quelques motifs de satisfaction, après les déceptions des Jeux de Paris et des Mondiaux 2025.

lemonde.title: Championnats du monde de badminton : la France se lance avec un « état d’esprit conquérant » pour confirmer son essor
lemonde.description: Un an après les Mondiaux à Paris, où l’équipe de France avait remporté une médaille de bronze, les badistes tricolores espèrent monter sur d’autres podiums lors de la compétition planétaire, qui se déroule du 17 au 23 août, à New Delhi.

lemonde.title: Grave épilepsie réfractaire chez un enfant : des années d’errance diagnostique après une simple griffure de chat
lemonde.description: L’histoire d’une traque hors norme. Des années d’investigations vont progressivement dévoiler un tableau clinique d’une étonnante complexité.

rfi.title: Cop17 aims to restore land and hope in fight against desertification
rfi.description: Extreme weather across much of Europe and elsewhere is lending added weight to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (Cop17), which begins on Monday in Mongolia. RFI looks at what's at stake worldwide.

rfi.title: Migrants stranded in Ceuta say ‘I’d rather die here than go back to Morocco’
rfi.description: Nearly three weeks after a mass border crossing brought tens of thousands of migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta, thousands remain stranded in precarious conditions, Maria Jimenez, spokesperson for the NGO Elin, told RFI. She said many still lack adequate shelter, food and medical care.

rfi.title: Devastated by wildfire, the village of Le Porge pins hopes for support on PM visit
rfi.description: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will visit the Gironde department in southwestern France on Monday to launch reconstruction efforts, after the area fell victim to the most destructive wildfires seen in 70 years. The mayor of Le Porge – one of the villages worst affected – told RFI he's hoping for government support to rebuild its economy, which relies heavily on forest exploitation.

rfi.title: Cameroon beat Malawi to claim maiden Women’s Cup of Nations title
rfi.description: Cameroon claimed a first Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) title when they beat Malawi 3-0 in Sunday's final in Morocco, with Marie Ngah Manga’s first-half double helping the the Indomitable Lionesses seal victory.

rfi.title: Ex-PM Attal urges Macron to put under-15 social media ban to referendum
rfi.description: Gabriel Attal has called on President Emmanuel Macron to put a proposed ban on social media for children under 15 directly to French voters, after the Constitutional Council struck down legislation approved by parliament.

rfi.title: Belgium turns to European air support as wildfire rages near German border
rfi.description: Belgium called in aerial reinforcements from across Europe on Sunday as firefighters battled the country’s largest wildfire in more than a century, with flames spreading rapidly through a difficult-to-reach nature reserve near the German border.

rfi.title: Europe's shrinking rivers give rise to debate over how to tackle drought
rfi.description: Europe's shrinking rivers are disrupting industry, reducing power generation and intensifying the debate over how to respond to worsening drought. As water levels fall across the continent, authorities and businesses alike are looking for ways to keep freight moving and critical infrastructure operating. Hydrologists warn, however, that digging rivers deeper cannot create more water and could make shortages worse.

rfi.title: Solar-powered community gardens offer lifeline in drought-hit Zimbabwe
rfi.description: At a shared garden in eastern Zimbabwe, solar-powered pumps are helping farmers grow crops year round, even when drought dries out other fields.

rfi.title: Obesity rises sharply as French Polynesia faces chronic health challenges
rfi.description: French Polynesia is facing growing public health pressures as rising rates of chronic disease combine with an ageing population and changing lifestyles. More than half of adult residents are now considered obese.

rfi.title: Morocco arrests nearly 300 migrants near Ceuta amid renewed crossing fears
rfi.description: Scores of would-be migrants, most of them from sub-Saharan Africa, were intercepted in northern Morocco near the border with the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Saturday, two weeks after tens of thousands of people attempted to enter the territory.

rfi.title: France probes unprecedented cyberattack after tax data of 678,000 users stolen
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a major cyberattack on the country’s tax administration that affected nearly 700,000 individuals and businesses, authorities said on Saturday.

rfi.title: France's successive heatwaves show strain of living in urban 'heat islands'
rfi.description: As France experiences its latest heatwave, residents of urban "heat islands" – dense neighbourhoods with few trees or green spaces – are suffering acutely in the high temperatures, and local authorities are searching for solutions.

rfi.title: Algeria edge Morocco on penalties in WAFCON third-place play-off
rfi.description: Morocco endured a second painful penalty shootout defeat in the space of four days as Algeria claimed third place at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations on Saturday following a 1-1 draw in Rabat.

rfi.title: Armenian Genocide survivors' grandson says 'political motives' block recognition
rfi.description: In 1915, the Ottoman Empire began the systematic deportation and massacre of its Armenian population. As many as 1.5 million Armenians were killed – widely regarded by historians as the twentieth century's first genocide, and the event for which the term was later coined. Stephan Pechdimaldji, the grandson of two of the survivors, spoke to RFI about why recognition still matters.

rfi.title: Nine killed in Israeli strikes on Lebanon as tensions test peace framework
rfi.description: At least nine people were killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon on Saturday, according to Lebanon’s state news agency, in some of the deadliest attacks since Beirut agreed to a US-mediated framework aimed at ending the latest round of fighting.

rfi.title: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghanistan seeks to ease international isolation
rfi.description: In the five years since the Taliban seized back power in Afghanistan, the country's worsening human rights record has drawn sanctions and aid cuts. But despite refusing to officially recognise the fundamentalist movement's government, some countries are concluding that engaging with the Taliban has become unavoidable.

rfi.title: In Turkey, one of the world's longest conflicts reaches a turning point
rfi.description: Turkey stands on the threshold of closing a conflict spanning almost 50 years, after the Turkish parliament this week passed a law allowing exiled Kurdish militants to return home and rejoin society. The legislation aims to end the war with the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which has battled the Turkish state for independence since 1984.

rfi.title: Law on assisted dying wins constitutional approval in France
rfi.description: France's Constitutional Council on Friday approved a law creating a right to assisted dying, removing the last major legal obstacle before the measure can be enacted and implemented.

euronews.description: Virgin Trains has been cleared to run up to 20 daily return services through the Channel Tunnel from 2030, bringing an end to Eurostar’s long-running monopoly one step closer.

euronews.title: Hundreds of nostalgic Germans flock to see Angela Merkel’s portrait

The painting has sparked reflections on Merkel’s 16 years in power, with some visitors expressing nostalgia.

euronews.description: The EU is to propose more “far-reaching” sanctions against Russia this autumn after the bloc’s latest package was watered down amid pressure to protect national economic interests.

euronews.title: 'Such devastating news': Stars pay tribute to Heroes and Scream star Hayden Panettiere, dead aged 36
euronews.description: Panettiere was best known for her role as cheerleader Claire Bennet in Heroes and country singer Juliette Barnes in Nashville. Stars of cinema and TV, and Hayden Panettiere's fans, have been paying tribute to the actress, who died aged 36. The cause of her death remains unknown for the time being.

euronews.title: Exclusive: Brussels keen to monitor UFOs under the radar
euronews.description: Brussels has signalled it is monitoring unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) and has hinted at improving capabilities, according to documents seen by Euronews.

euronews.title: Europe wildfires: German border town partially evacuated but France blaze stabilised
euronews.description: A historically hot summer on the planet's fastest-warming continent has contributed to the deaths of thousands of people and increased the risk of wildfires, with blazes periodically sweeping through parched landscapes.

euronews.title: Belgium races to tame huge wildfire 'spreading towards Germany'
euronews.description: Firefighters battle the advancing flames in eastern Belgium as thick smoke and difficult terrain complicate efforts to contain the blaze.

france24fr.title: Corée du Sud : Trump réduit la participation américaine aux exercices militaires
france24fr.description: Donald Trump annonce une forte réduction de la participation américaine aux exercices militaires avec la Corée du Sud, invoquant leur coût et sa "très bonne relation" avec Kim Jong-un.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : à Saint-Louis, les régates perpétuent une tradition séculaire
france24fr.description: À Saint-Louis, dans le nord du Sénégal, les régates de pirogues, héritées des pêcheurs de Guet-Ndar, rassemblent des milliers de personnes autour d’une tradition séculaire. Une course devenue un véritable marqueur de l’identité de la ville. "Nous avons hérité cette course de nos aïeux et maintenant, c’est à nous de perpétuer ce legs", souligne le régatier Ismaïla Sakho.

france24fr.title: Italie : quatre oeuvres d'Antonello de Messine volées dans un musée sicilien
france24fr.description: Quatre oeuvres "d'une valeur exceptionnelle" du célèbre peintre de la Renaissance Antonello de Messine ont été dérobées dans un musée en Sicile, a annoncé dimanche le ministère italien de la Culture dans un communiqué.

france24fr.title: Le parquet de Paris ouvre une enquête sur le piratage massif du fisc
france24fr.description: "Extraction frauduleuse de données" et "association de malfaiteurs" : la section cyber du parquet de Paris a ouvert une enquête après la cyberattaque touchant près de 700.000 usagers de l'administration fiscale.

france24fr.title: Nouvelles frappes russo-ukrainiennes, plusieurs morts dans la région russe de Belgorod
france24fr.description: Au moins six personnes sont mortes dans une frappe de missiles ukrainiens dans la région russe de Belgorod, près de la frontière, ont annoncé, lundi, les autorités locales, tandis que Kiev fait état d'attaques russes dans la région d'Odessa. L'Ukraine et la Russie sont entraînées dans une nette escalade depuis plusieurs semaines.

france24fr.title: Incendie en Belgique : la progression du feu "limitée", des moyens aériens mobilisés
france24fr.description: L'incendie en Belgique n'est pas encore fixé lundi mais sa "progression est restée limitée" grâce à "des vents plus favorables et aux précipitations enregistrées en fin de nuit", ont indiqué les autorités dans un communiqué.

france24fr.title: Exercices militaires avec Séoul : Trump annonce une réduction "considérable"
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a annoncé "réduire considérablement" la participation des Etats-Unis aux exercices militaires annuels avec la Corée du Sud qui ont débuté lundi, invoquant en particulier sa "très bonne relation avec Kim Jong Un", le dirigeant nord-coréen.

france24fr.title: Kinshasa : la SAPE à l'honneur lors de la 6e édition de la DRC Fashion Week
france24fr.description: La sixième édition de la DRC Fashion Week s'est déroulée ce samedi à Kinshasa, réunissant des stylistes, des créateurs de mode et des « sapeurs » de la République démocratique du Congo et de la République du Congo voisine. Objectif : fusionner les cultures communes des deux Congo en mettant à l'honneur la musique et la « SAPE » (Société des ambianceurs et des personnes élégantes, à savoir un mouvement culturel et vestimentaire centré sur le dandysme.

france24fr.title: Le Cameroun remporte la première CAN féminine de son histoire
france24fr.description: Le Cameroun a remporté dimanche la première Coupe d'Afrique des nations féminine de son histoire, en surclassant en finale un Malawi novice (3-0) dans une affiche surprise à Rabat (Maroc).

france24fr.title: Trump veut réduire fortement les exercices militaires avec la Corée du Sud
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a annoncé "réduire considérablement" la participation des Etats-Unis aux exercices militaires annuels avec la Corée du Sud qui ont débuté lundi, invoquant en particulier sa "très bonne relation avec Kim Jong Un", le dirigeant nord-coréen.

france24fr.title: Indonésie : des milliers d'évacués en attente d'aide après le puissant séisme
france24fr.description: Des milliers de personnes évacuées attendent dimanche de l'aide au lendemain du puissant séisme qui a secoué l'île indonésienne de Florès (est), faisant 53 morts, des dizaines de blessés et endommageant des centaines de bâtiments.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : l'ONU achemine de l'aide humanitaire dans des maisons assiégées
france24fr.description: Une équipe des Nations unies réussit à acheminer de la nourriture et des médicaments à trois familles toujours assiégées dans le village de Qusra, où les forces israéliennes ont imposé un bouclage total autour des trois maisons que les colons tentent, depuis huit jours, de s’approprier et dont ils cherchent à expulser les propriétaires palestiniens. Les forces israéliennes sont toujours déployées à l’intérieur et aux abords de ces maisons et patrouillent dans le village de Qusra.

france24fr.title: Après le Hamas, Jared Kushner va s'entretenir avec Netanyahu au sujet de Gaza
france24fr.description: Jared ⁠Kushner, émissaire américain ​et gendre du président Donald Trump, doit rencontrer lundi le Premier ministre israélien ​Benjamin Netanyahu dans le but de faire avancer le plan de paix pour Gaza, au lendemain d'une rencontre exceptionnelle avec des responsables du Hamas au Caire.

france24fr.title: Marchand magistral, premier sacre des Lionnes et Lens vainqueur du PSG : les infos sport du week-end
france24fr.description: Léon Marchand qui fait sensation aux Championnats d'Europe de natation, le Cameroun sacré pour la première fois de son histoire après sa victoire face au Malawi en finale de la CAN féminine, et le RC Lens qui remporte le Trophée des Champions face au PSG : voici ce qu'il ne fallait pas manquer dans les infos sport de ce week-end.

france24fr.title: L'épidémie d'Ebola devient la plus meurtrière de l'histoire de la RD Congo
france24fr.description: Le bilan de l'épidémie d'Ebola qui sévit en République démocratique du Congo vient de dépasser celui de la précédente flambée (2018-2020), avec plus de 2 300 morts, selon les autorités congolaises, lundi. Plusieurs vaccins sont à l'essai contre la souche du virus actuel. L'OMS espère inverser la tendance dans le pays d'ici trois mois.

france24fr.title: Alvin Junior Mak, étoile montante de la mode franco-congolaise propulsé par le Mondial
france24fr.description: Innovation africaine (3/3). Styliste franco-congolais, Alvin Junior Mak a marqué de son empreinte le Mondial de football en concevant le très remarqué costume de l'équipe de la République du Congo. Un succès fulgurant accueilli avec enthousiasme mais sans triomphalisme par le jeune prodige de la mode, qui perçoit son travail comme une course de fond et non un sprint.

france24fr.title: Trophée des champions : à 10 contre 11, Lens fait tomber le PSG
france24fr.description: Le RC Lens a remporté le Trophée des champions face au Paris Saint-Germain (1-0). Sous les yeux de Zinédine Zidane, les Lensois ont tenu une heure en infériorité numérique.

france24fr.title: L'actrice américaine Hayden Panettiere, star de "Heroes", meurt à l'âge de 36 ans
france24fr.description: L'actrice américaine Hayden Panettiere, connue pour ses rôles dans les séries télévisées "Heroes" et "Nashville", est morte à l'âge de 36 ans. Son décès a été annoncé par des médias dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi.

zeit.title: Demokratische Republik Kongo: Ebola-Virus breitet sich im Ostkongo rasant aus
zeit.description: Durch den Ebolavirus sind bereits mehr als 2.300 Menschen in der DR Kongo gestorben. Der aktuelle Ebola-Ausbruch ist der tödlichste in der Geschichte des Landes.

zeit.title: Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: Maier: AfD darf Daten zur Spionage-Abwehr nicht einsehen
Nach wochenlanger Trockenheit: Wetterdienst warnt vor schweren Gewittern in Schwaben
Neues Schuljahr: Polizei rät: Schulweg gemeinsam üben vor dem ersten Schultag
Rochade in der Bundesregierung: CDU-Landeschef bedauert Absage von Fast-Minister an Merz
Gesellschaftliches Risiko: Jeder zehnte junge Mensch nicht in Bildung oder Arbeit
Rasanter Anstieg: Ebola-Ausbruch ist tödlichster in der Geschichte des Kongo
In Probe nachgewiesen: Blaualgen im Neckar nachgewiesen: Landkreis rät vom Baden ab
Industrie im Aufwind: Sachsen-Anhalts Industrie steigert Umsatz und Aufträge
Frankreich: Frankreichs Premierminister verteidigt Vorgehen bei Waldbränden
zeit.description: »Wir haben nichts zu verbergen«, sagte der französische Premierminister bei einem Besuch in einem Brandgebiet nahe Bordeaux. Dort war er von Anwohnenden ausgebuht worden.

zeit.title: Aggressivität im Straßenverkehr: Aggression im Straßenverkehr nimmt Langzeitstudie zufolge zu
zeit.description: Immer mehr Verkehrsteilnehmer räumen ein, sich im Straßenverkehr teilweise aggressiv zu verhalten. Forscher sehen gestiegenen Druck als einen möglichen Grund.

zeit.title: Freiwillige Ausreisen: Zahl der freiwilligen Ausreisen abgelehnter Asylsuchender gestiegen
zeit.description: Mehr abgelehnte Asylbewerber kehren freiwillig in ihre Herkunftsländer zurück. Seit Jahresbeginn sind knapp 10.000 Migranten freiwillig aus Deutschland ausgereist.

zeit.title: Kinderfotos: Fotografieren wir die Kindheit kaputt?
zeit.description: Die Generation Alpha wird so viel fotografiert wie keine andere Generation zuvor. Doch auf der Suche nach dem perfekten Bild verpassen Eltern die besten Momente.

zeit.title: Taiwan-Konflikt: Taiwans Regierung plant 2027 Rekordausgaben für die Verteidigung
zeit.description: Das höhere Militärbudget zeige die Entschiedenheit Taiwans, seine Verteidigung auszubauen, sagte Präsident Lai. Derweil nimmt der Druck aus Festlandchina weiter zu.

zeit.title: Europäische Union: Apple ändert in der EU die Abfrage zu App-Tracking
zeit.description: Die Abfrage auf Apple-Geräten, ob Nutzer der Verarbeitung von Daten in Apps zustimmen, stieß seit Längerem auf Kritik. Nun wird die Gestaltung der Auswahlseite angepasst.

spiegel.title: NBA: Dennis Schröder wechselt zu den Charlotte Hornets
spiegel.description: Neue Saison, neues Team: Damit kennt sich Dennis Schröder aus. Mit dem Wechsel zu den Hornets steht er kurz vor dem Rekord für die meisten NBA-Teams. In Charlotte hofft er vor allem auf mehr Spielzeit.

spiegel.title: Irland: Fünf Teenager sterben bei Verkehrsunfall
spiegel.description: Sie waren mit ihrem Fahrzeug in die falsche Richtung unterwegs: Fünf Teenager sind in Irland bei einem schweren Verkehrsunfall ums Leben gekommen. Ihr Fahrzeug war Medienberichten zufolge gestohlen.

spiegel.title: Aggression im Straßenverkehr: Jeder zweite Autofahrer reagiert sich sofort ab
spiegel.description: Drängeln, offensives Einscheren, Smartphone am Steuer: Autofahrer auf deutschen Straßen verhalten sich einer Studie zufolge immer problematischer. Radfahrer kommen in der Erhebung kaum besser weg.

spiegel.title: Gillian Anderson spricht über ihre Liebesbeziehungen zu Frauen
spiegel.description: »Es fühlte sich geheimnisvoll, illegal und falsch an«: Gillian Anderson hat über die Beziehung zu einer Frau in ihrer Jugend gesprochen. Obwohl diese heimlich gewesen sei, habe sie ihr noch Jahre später Probleme bereitet.

spiegel.title: Deutschland: Jeder zehnte junge Erwachsene ist ohne Job oder Ausbildung
spiegel.description: Mehr 20- bis 24-Jährige in Deutschland haben weder einen Job noch eine Ausbildung. Wie Daten des Statistischen Bundesamtes zeigen, sind Frauen und Großstädte stärker betroffen – der EU-Schnitt liegt sogar noch höher.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM in Birmingham: Das deutsche Team liefert, der Veranstalter nicht
spiegel.description: Mit einer exzellenten Bilanz beenden die deutschen Athletinnen und Athleten die Europameisterschaft. Die sportlichen Leistungen in Birmingham waren beachtlich – die Rahmenbedingungen häufig nicht.

spiegel.title: Südkorea: Regierung setzt trotz Trump-Kritik auf enge Kooperation mit USA
spiegel.description: Donald Trump hat angekündigt, US-südkoreanische Militärübungen einzuschränken. Doch Seoul hält an der engen Zusammenarbeit mit Washington fest. Währenddessen setzt Nordkorea seine Raketentests fort.

spiegel.title: AstraZeneca: Pharmakonzern stoppt wichtige Studie zu Lungenkrebs-Mittel
spiegel.description: Pharmariese AstraZeneca musste eine Studie für ein wichtiges Lungenkrebsmedikament stoppen. Es ist nicht der erste Fehlschlag in der jüngsten Zeit.

spiegel.title: AfD: Wie sie sich als neue Arbeiterpartei inszeniert
spiegel.description: Die AfD umwirbt Menschen mit kleinen Einkommen, die früher noch SPD gewählt hätten. Ihre Versprechen an die Arbeiter wird die Partei aber kaum einlösen können.

spiegel.title: Tropensturm »Lala« sorgt für Zerstörung auf Hawaii
spiegel.description: Umgestürzte Bäume, Straßensperren, Stromausfälle: Ausläufer des Tropensturms »Lala« haben Hawaiis Hauptinsel Big Island getroffen. Bei einem Autounfall starb ein Mensch.

spiegel.title: Dortmund: 13-Jähriger angefahren – Polizei ermittelt gegen Fahrer wegen Verdachts auf illegales Autorennen
spiegel.description: Zwei Männer sollen sich in Dortmund ein illegales Autorennen geliefert und dabei einen Teenager verletzt haben. Von der Polizei hieß es dazu: »Das war ganz knapp an der Vollkatastrophe vorbei.«

spiegel.title: Migration und das Drama von Ceuta: Wenn Mitgefühl als Sicherheitsrisiko gilt
spiegel.description: Nicht ein Mensch hat den europäischen Kontinent erreicht. In der Debatte über Ceuta scheint die Frage nach den Fluchtgründen keine Rolle mehr spielen zu dürfen. Ein fataler Reflex.

spiegel.title: Tony Marshall: Was bleibt heute von der Schlagerikone und der Unterhaltungswelt, in der er sich bewegte?
spiegel.description: Herbert Nold war 44 Jahre lang der Manager von Tony Marshall. Was bleibt heute von der Schlagerikone und der Unterhaltungswelt, in der er sich bewegte?

spiegel.title: Waldbrand in Belgien: Feuer rückt nicht weiter Richtung Deutschland vor
spiegel.description: Die Feuerwehren kämpfen weiter gegen den Brand im Naturschutzgebiet Hohes Venn in Belgien. Die Bundeswehr schickt Löschhubschrauber. Grund zur Hoffnung gibt es für die Einwohner von Monschau in der Eifel.

spiegel.title: USA unter Trump: Wie der Kampf gegen KI Demokraten und Republikaner spaltet
spiegel.description: Künstliche Intelligenz wird zum entscheidenden Wahlkampfthema in den USA. Während Trump auf schnelles Wachstum setzt, profilieren sich progressive Demokraten und einige Republikaner als Kämpfer gegen die Techkonzerne.

spiegel.title: Fast jeder zehnte Euro der Haushalte fließt in Freizeitausgaben
spiegel.description: Die verbreitete Krisenstimmung, hohe Mieten und teurer Sprit konnten den Trend nicht bremsen. Die Deutschen geben immer mehr für ihre Freizeitbeschäftigungen aus.

spiegel.title: Immobilien-Krise: Ifo-Studie meldet mehr Baugenehmigungen und mehr Stornos
spiegel.description: Die gestiegene Zahl der Baugenehmigungen weckt Hoffnungen auf einen Aufschwung im Immobiliensektor. Dabei ist das Ende der Talsohle noch nicht einmal in Sicht.

spiegel.title: Waldbrände in Deutschland und Belgien: Feuer bei Schramberg weitet sich aus, leichtes Aufatmen im Westerwald
spiegel.description: Waldbrände halten die Einsatzkräfte in Atem: Bei Schramberg in Baden-Württemberg erschwert das Gelände das Löschen. Im Hohen Venn in Belgien unterstützt die Bundeswehr. Aus Waldaschaff gibt es gute Nachrichten.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Ciao, ciao, Sonderfall – die Schweiz und der Sommer der unangenehmen Erkenntnisse
nzz.description: Dürre, eine Armee, die das Land nur wenige Wochen verteidigen kann, und gnadenloses Powerplay der Grossmächte. In der Schweiz kommen gerade einige Überzeugungen ins Wanken.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Grösstes Wildberries-Logistikzentrum bei Moskau in Brand+++ Mutmasslich russische Drohne über Rumänien abgeschossen
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Der Vincenz-Prozess geht in die zweite Woche: Die Verteidigung spricht von «absurden und zynischen» Vorwürfen
nzz.description: Im Zentrum des Berufungsprozesses steht die Frage, ob die gegen Pierin Vincenz verhängte langjährige Freiheitsstrafe gerechtfertigt ist oder nicht. Ab Montag plädieren die Verteidiger der weiteren Beschuldigten.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - So teuer ist Ihr Einkauf bei Aldi, Rewe und Co. geworden
nzz.description: Sie haben das Gefühl, alles wird teurer? Vergleichen Sie Ihren Kassenzettel von heute mit dem gleichen Einkauf von 2022 in deutschen Supermärkten – und erleben Sie Ihren persönlichen Preisschock.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Waffenruhe im Gazastreifen: Israels Polizeiminister Ben-Gvir will täglich Dutzende Tötungen von Palästinensern
nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Travail Suisse verlangt «generelle Lohnerhöhungen» von 2 Prozent für 2027
KURZMELDUNGEN - Kultur: Schauspielerin Hayden Panettiere 36-jährig gestorben
DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: Die aktuelle Epidemie erweist sich als die tödlichste in Kongo-Kinshasas Geschichte
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation (WHO) hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Die Infektionszahlen steigen weiterhin an. Hier sind die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebola-Virus zu finden.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: USA fahren Militärübungen mit Südkorea zurück
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Politiker lieben die Mehrwertsteuer – genau deshalb sollte sie dringend reformiert werden
nzz.description: Der Bund will die Mehrwertsteuer in der Schweiz stark erhöhen. Damit nehmen auch Verzerrungen zu, die Wirtschaft und Wohlstand belasten. Es braucht endlich einen Einheitssatz.

nzz.title: Faten steigt am 29. Juli in Marokko ins Meer, wenig später ist sie tot. Besuch bei einer Familie, die Antworten sucht
nzz.description: Von einem Gerücht, das mit dem Tod endete.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Deutschland droht ein Prekariat bei Jugendlichen. Das hat auch mit der Einwanderung zu tun
nzz.description: Viele junge Menschen in Deutschland haben keinen Berufsabschluss. Das ist eine bildungspolitische Bankrotterklärung und eine fatale Wachstumsbremse. Die Regierung muss handeln. Dazu gehört auch, den Mindestlohn abzuschaffen.

nzz.title: Vier Wochen, mehr als zwanzig brennende Logistikzentren: Ukrainische Drohnen verursachen in Russland riesige Schäden, aber noch keine Wirtschaftskrise
nzz.description: Durch einen ukrainischen Luftangriff ist bei Moskau das grösste Warenlager des Onlinehändlers Wildberries in Flammen aufgegangen. Die unmittelbaren militärischen Folgen sind gering, aber die Ukraine hofft vor allem auf eine wirtschaftliche Kettenreaktion.

nzz.title: China startet die kommerzielle Containerschifffahrt durch die Arktis
nzz.description: Wegen des hohen Ölpreises und des Klimawandels beginnen sich Schiffstransporte entlang der Nordroute von Asien nach Europa für Reedereien zu lohnen. Doch die Fahrten durchs Eismeer bergen Risiken.

nzz.title: Verhandeln unter Aufsicht: Die USA beginnen das nächste Kapitel in ihrem Machtspiel in Venezuela
nzz.description: Sind die Gespräche zwischen Regime und Opposition in Caracas eine Farce, oder gibt es eine reale Chance auf Wandel? Klar ist, dass die Regierung Trump ihre eigenen Interessen verfolgt.

observador.title: Trump quer menos exercícios com Coreia do Sul, um "desastre"
observador.description: Trump deu instruções a Hegseth para reduzir exercícios militares que decorrem há mais de 70 anos entre Washington e Seul. Presidência sul-coreana avalia caso e oposição fala em "desastre diplomático".

observador.title: Ordem saúda adiamento de novo sistema de acesso a consultas
observador.description: Ordem aprecia adiamento, que considera "decisão prudente e responsável", visto que o sistema ainda se encontra em fase de testes. Assinala que reforma só funciona quando preparada com rigor.

observador.title: Liechtenstein muda regras de sucessão ao trono
observador.description: Era o único país europeu onde o trono era exclusivo dos homens. A câmara aprovou a alteração com maioria de dois terços, mas o impacto real só se sentirá daqui a pelo menos duas gerações.

observador.title: MP acusa Rui Cristina de discriminação e incitamento ao ódio
observador.description: Caso remonta a novembro de 2025, quando Rui Cristina afirmou não destinar qualquer quantia para dar habitação a "cidadãos locais pertencentes a uma determinada etnia".

observador.title: PM britânico troca mensagens com falsa conselheira de Trump
observador.description: Andy Burnham contactou uma pessoa que se fez passar por Susie Wiles, a quem enviou algumas mensagens "sem importância". O telemóvel da republicana já fora pirateado em maio de 2025.

observador.title: Bélgica. Chuva trava avanço do "maior incêndio da história"
observador.description: Vento favorável e primeiras chuvas travaram o avanço das chamas em Hautes Fagnes. Dois helicópteros militares da Alemanha chegaram ao território belga para reforçar as operações de combate às chamas.

observador.title: ONU estima 500 combatentes insurgentes em Cabo Delgado
observador.description: ONU destaca que grupo terrorista "intensificou os esforços de recrutamento", apesar de esforços militares. Extorsão no mar e raptos são as principais fontes de rendimento, para movimentar dinheiro.

observador.title: “Se a legislatura não tiver condições, é preferível mudar”
observador.description: Carlos Zorrinho, presidente da Câmara de Évora, quer a legislatura cumprida se houver rumo, no entanto exige reformas urgentes no poder local, com regionalização e nova lei das finanças locais.

observador.title: Benfica procura primeira vitória frente ao Casa Pia
observador.description: No encerramento da segunda jornada, o clube encarnado procura a vitória frente aos "gansos", que vêm de derrota por 1-0 contra o Marítimo. Arouca e "verde-rubros" surpreendem, com 6 pontos cada.

observador.title: Homem detido por agressões à companheira perante filhos
observador.description: Detido em flagrante delito, está "fortemente indiciado" por maus-tratos à mulher desde o início da relação, em 2022. Está, desde abril, a cumprir pena suspensa por crime a outra vítima.

observador.title: Europeus Atletismo. Sentimento agridoce por não haver ouro
observador.description: Presidente da Federação de Atletismo lamenta que alguns atletas não tenham ficado no 1º lugar, mas saúda as medalhas conquistadas. Domingos Castro fala de uma "geração de ouro" para os Jogos Olímpicos

observador.title: 10h. Incêndio em Boticas está dominado
observador.description: Apesar dos quase 300 operacionais que estão no terreno, 80 veículos e quatro meios aéreos o incêndio já está controlado. Ainda, mais uma noite de troca de ataques entre Rússia e Ucrânia.

observador.title: Surto de ébola é o segundo mais letal de sempre
observador.description: O surto supera, tanto em contágios como mortes, o surto que atingiu o país entre 2018 e 2020. A epidemia está a espalhar-se rapidamente, perante greves, ameaças de grupos rebeldes e desinformação.

observador.title: Campanha "Taxa Zero ao Volante" a partir de terça-feira
observador.description: A ANSR ficará a cargo das ações de sensibilização, enquanto as forças de segurança estarão encarregadas das operações de fiscalização. Alertam para condução sob efeito de álcool.

observador.title: Vai de férias? A segurança começa no carro
observador.description: Pneus, travões, luzes, documentos e pausas: sabe tudo a que deve estar atento antes de fazer uma viagem? Damos uma ajuda.

observador.title: Rentrée do Estado na REN vai baixar o preço da eletricidade?
observador.description: Luís Montengro anunciou no Pontal a reentrada do Estado na REN com dois objetivos bem definidos. O PS diz que não vão ser cumpridos, o Chega levanta dúvidas e o PSD lembra o contexto europeu.

observador.title: Montenegro e Carneiro estão presos ao passado?
observador.description: Montenegro e Carneiro voltaram das férias com discursos inspirados no passado. Entre Cavaco e Guterres isto é a prova que a política nacional anda a ser uma bela viagem aos anos 90.

observador.title: Nove distritos sob aviso laranja até terça-feira
observador.description: O IPMA colocou também vários distritos sob aviso amarelo até às 18h00 de terça-feira e prevê uma continuação de tempo quente com céu pouco nublado no continente.

phys-org.title: The Nigerian fishing community being eaten up by the Atlantic

phys-org.title: Hawaii recovery efforts begin as Lala is downgraded, moves west
phys-org.description: Clean-up efforts were underway Sunday as Hurricane Lala, which was downgraded to a tropical storm, rolled past Hawaii's Big Island and dumped heavy rain across the U.S. Pacific state.

phys-org.title: Giant crocodylians dominated the food chain in Miocene South America, fossil evidence suggests
phys-org.description: South America was a frightening place during the Miocene. More than 10 million years ago, a vast lake covered much of the continent, home to giant turtles and crocodylians.

phys-org.title: Flightless beetles evolved distinct snail-hunting shapes on Japan's largest island
phys-org.description: Islands are widely recognized as natural laboratories of evolution. The ocean restricts movement among islands, allowing isolated populations to adapt to different environments and, at times, diverge into new species. However, on large islands, geographic distance may restrict movement, while environmental variation may impose divergent selection, thereby promoting adaptive divergence. Does adaptive divergence occur not only among islands but also within islands?

phys-org.title: Radio telescopes help scientists map molecules in space and uncover where and how stars form
phys-org.description: You may have heard the phrase "we are made of star-stuff." This statement by the astronomer Carl Sagan refers to the fact that elements heavier than hydrogen and helium were forged in the centers of the first stars. But how does this star-stuff evolve into the chemistry of rocks, plants and people?

phys-org.title: Brief firearm safety talks more than double openness to out-of-home storage
phys-org.description: A brief chat about firearm safety can sharply increase willingness among gun owners to consider temporarily storing their firearms outside the home during times of crisis, a step that could help reduce suicide risk, according to a Rutgers-led study.

phys-org.title: Hurricane Lala pulls away from Hawaii's Big Island
phys-org.description: Hurricane Lala was pulling away from Hawaii's Big Island early Sunday as heavy rain and strong winds struck the U.S. Pacific state and officials warned of potentially dangerous flooding.

phys-org.title: Belgium races to tame huge wildfire creeping toward Germany
phys-org.description: Water-bombing aircraft and farmers' tractors joined forces Sunday to help firefighters tame Belgium's largest modern-day wildfire, which has scorched vast swaths of a hard-to-reach nature reserve near the German border.

phys-org.title: Japan aims for the moons of Mars

phys-org.title: A small squeeze reveals new clues about an unusual kind of magnet
phys-org.description: Researchers at Rice University have found that gently squeezing a crystal of iron sulfide can change two of its unusual properties at the same time: its tiny magnetic signal and the way electricity moves through it. The result gives scientists a clearer picture of how a newly recognized class of magnetic materials works and suggests a simple way to control their behavior.

phys-org.title: Gene-edited beagles produce no detectable major dog allergen, early tests find
phys-org.description: Humans love dogs, but petting them can leave some people sneezing and wheezing. About 15% of the world's population lives with a dog allergy, which can increase the risk of hay fever and asthma. The main culprit is Can f 1, a protein found mainly in dog saliva. Right now, staying away from furry friends or getting regular immunotherapy shots or tablets is the only way to deal with the symptoms.

phys-org.title: Phytophthora dieback linked to habitat loss and lower digging activity among quendas in Western Australia
phys-org.description: A new study from Murdoch University has found that the introduced plant disease Phytophthora dieback is indirectly hindering quendas in Western Australia's jarrah forests by reducing their habitat quality and consequently decreasing their digging activity. The paper, "Exotic Plant Pathogen Reduces Habitat and Foraging Activities of a Digging Mammal," was published in the journal Austral Ecology.

phys-org.title: Strain flips Hall signal in altermagnetic manganese telluride, suggesting a path to practical spintronics
phys-org.description: Time-reversal symmetry is an exotic behavior found in systems whose internal physics looks different when running forward versus backward in time. For some time, physicists have searched for this behavior in systems with almost no overall magnetization. Such phases are highly prized for spintronics, where information is carried using the quantum spins of electrons.

phys-org.title: Chinese ship sets off for Europe through Arctic, halving travel time
phys-org.description: A Chinese container vessel has set sail for Europe through the Arctic as part of a new weekly service on a route that cuts shipment times in half but that environmental groups warn could speed up the melting of polar ice.

phys-org.title: Firefighters battle second day of blaze on Greek island
phys-org.description: Firefighters battled for a second day Sunday to contain a forest fire on the Greek Aegean island of Skyros, as the local mayor voiced hope it could soon be brought under control.

phys-org.title: Shrinking water bodies can turn drought into disease hotspots or dead ends
phys-org.description: Prolonged dry spells or droughts can sometimes reduce aquatic diseases, many of which affect people. Yet other times, water scarcity can counterintuitively lead to an uptick in diseases that depend on water.

phys-org.title: Einstein Probe catches rare X-ray flash from an exploding star
phys-org.description: Astronomers have linked an X-ray flash discovered by the Einstein Probe to a known type of supernova with unusual features that point to the birth of an ultra-dense, rapidly spinning magnetar. The paper outlining this finding was published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters on July 22.

phys-org.title: Active particles could make stable glasses stronger without catastrophic brittle failure
phys-org.description: The strongest glasses have an Achilles' heel that causes them to fail catastrophically when pushed past their limit. They do not bend or stretch, as all damage concentrates into a single plane and the material fails in an instant. This brittleness has long capped the usefulness of high-stability amorphous solids, from bulk metallic glasses to engineered metamaterials.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: What Should Be Done About Asia’s Undervalued Currencies?
proj-syn.description: Those who worry that the renminbi, yen, and won are undervalued vis-à-vis the dollar are usually focused on the large trade and current-account surpluses that China, Japan, and Korea run with the US. But coordinated intervention in currency markets will not address the fundamentals underlying these imbalances.

proj-syn.title: How Corporations Can Mitigate an AI Jobocalypse
proj-syn.description: Even if AI-related job displacement is less severe than many feared, corporations will need to be enlisted in minimizing its effects in the name of social solidarity. To that end, governments should consider what policy incentives are in place, and large employers should consider their own long-term interests.

proj-syn.title: The Making and Remaking of Chinese Totalitarianism
proj-syn.description: For decades, the West assumed that economic growth would turn China into a more open, liberal society, much as it did South Korea and Taiwan. Instead, China’s totalitarian institutions proved remarkably resilient, surviving decades of reform and reasserting themselves under President Xi Jinping.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Not Forget Multilateral Institutions
proj-syn.description: The roadmap for middle-power action that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb recently laid out calls for countries that share interests to create ad hoc coalitions. But to be effective, these coalitions must work as much as possible within existing multilateral institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Real Competitiveness Test
proj-syn.description: The balance of global investment has shifted dramatically over the past three decades, with China emerging as the leading destination for productive capital. Europe and the United States can still narrow the gap, but only by making it cheaper and easier to build, operate, and innovate.

proj-syn.title: Our AI, Your Problem
proj-syn.description: The debate over whether European firms should use a Chinese state-directed model or one built by a private US firm threatens to distract from Europe’s most pressing problem, which is that it has no seat at either table. To preserve its own sovereignty, the continent must create a third option for itself.

proj-syn.title: Chile’s Boring Conservative President
proj-syn.description: Rather than governing like a pugnacious populist or a ruthless pragmatist, Chile’s new president, José Antonio Kast, has adopted an old-school center-right agenda and governing style reminiscent of the 1980s. Yet even this potentially safer approach comes with its own risks and costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe Failed the Ceuta Test
proj-syn.description: The current migration crisis is eating away at the solidarity on which the European Union depends, fueling the rise of the far right and pushing leaders to adopt increasingly hardline policies. But the Ceuta debacle shows why such measures cannot address the deeper forces driving migration.

proj-syn.title: The Legacy of Zhu Rongji
proj-syn.description: Zhu Rongji’s personal history and political challenges made it highly unlikely that he would rise to the pinnacle of Chinese politics. Once there, he implemented many of the reforms that turned the country into an economic powerhouse.

proj-syn.title: The Twilight of the ICC
proj-syn.description: Born amid the euphoria of the West’s Cold War victory, the International Criminal Court embodied the aspiration that international law could transcend politics. But the ICC always represented victors’ justice, and it was never equipped to operate in a world shaped by Machtpolitik.

proj-syn.title: Will Latin America Embrace Guerrilla Geopolitics?
proj-syn.description: The resurgence of guerrilla warfare in Ukraine and Iran has underscored the potential benefits of asymmetric action in today’s increasingly multipolar world. Latin America, in particular, should consider how to leverage its many strengths to remedy its relatively weak position on the global stage.

proj-syn.title: China’s Biggest Weakness on AI
proj-syn.description: When a state can credibly promise that labor displacement will not mean destitution, workers and their representatives are more likely to accept technological change. But since China can promise no such thing, its lack of a robust welfare state has emerged as a fundamental weakness in the broader AI race.

proj-syn.title: The Monetary Roots of Political Extremism
proj-syn.description: While the global economy generates unprecedented wealth for plutocrats like Elon Musk, it is, by design, highly unequal, dangerously over-indebted, prone to recurring financial crises, and ecologically disastrous. In such a context, radical reforms will be needed, beginning with the rejection of money as a commodity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Rise of the Token Economy
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.
